name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Gallbladder and Extrahepatic Biliary Tract
aliases: Extrahepatic Biliary Tract Squamous Cell Carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Gallbladder and Biliary Tract Carcinomas

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of squamous cell carcinoma in gallbladder or extrahepatic biliary tract tissue
Radiological evidence of mass lesion in gallbladder or extrahepatic biliary tract on ultrasound, CT, or MRI
Presence of obstructive jaundice or biliary colic symptoms consistent with biliary tract malignancy
Elevated serum CA 19-9 or CEA levels supporting malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological confirmation of squamous cell carcinoma combined with radiological evidence of tumor in gallbladder or extrahepatic biliary tract
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of metastatic squamous cell carcinoma from other primary sites.

pathognomonic.notes: Yellowing of skin and sclera due to bile duct obstruction
Mass detected on physical examination in gallbladder region
searchTerms: lump felt in right upper belly

common.notes: Dull or colicky pain related to tumor invasion or biliary obstruction
Significant weight loss over weeks to months
Loss of appetite associated with malignancy
Itching due to bile salt accumulation

occasional.notes: Low-grade fever possibly due to tumor necrosis or cholangitis
Gastrointestinal upset secondary to biliary obstruction
Resulting from lack of bile pigments in stool

rare.notes: Enlarged liver due to tumor infiltration or metastasis
Fluid accumulation in peritoneal cavity from advanced disease
Enlarged lymph nodes due to metastatic spread

laboratory: Increased alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT)
Elevated tumor markers CA 19-9 and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA)
imaging: Ultrasound showing gallbladder mass or bile duct obstruction
Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI demonstrating tumor extent and local invasion
MRCP (Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography) showing biliary tract obstruction
genetic: No specific genetic mutations consistently identified; molecular profiling may reveal TP53 mutations or EGFR overexpression
other: Histopathology revealing keratinizing squamous cells with intercellular bridges and keratin pearls
Endoscopic biopsy or surgical specimen required for definitive diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Histology showing glandular differentiation rather than squamous features
More common than squamous cell carcinoma
Arises from bile duct epithelium with adenocarcinoma histology
Different tumor marker profile and imaging characteristics

redFlags: Palpable abdominal mass in right upper quadrant
Unexplained significant weight loss and anorexia
references: Bridgewater J, Galle PR, Khan SA, et al. Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. J Hepatol. 2014;60(6):1268-1289.
Hundal R, Shaffer EA. Gallbladder cancer: epidemiology and outcome. Clin Epidemiol. 2014;6:99-109.
Khan SA, Thomas HC, Davidson BR, Taylor-Robinson SD. Cholangiocarcinoma. Lancet. 2005;366(9493):1303-1314.
